packages.title: DfT Electric vehicle charging infrastructure data tables (EVCI) — scope and status QA
facts: DfT published the EVCI data-table page on 26 February 2026 and updated it on 21 May 2026.
The tables include public EV charger statistics and grant-scheme statistics.
The 1 April 2026 tables include public chargers by country and region and by local authority and county.
Infrastructure counts and grant records must remain distinct from measured emissions.
No cadastral or property-level greenhouse-gas value is derived from EVCI tables.

packages.title: Environment Agency Pollution Inventory — scope and status QA
facts: The Environment Agency Pollution Inventory dataset page was last updated on 17 April 2026.
It provides downloadable data for years 2013 to 2024.
The inventory collates annual mass releases to air, controlled waters and sewers and waste transfers from large regulated industrial sites.
Reporting covers the whole authorisation or permit and can include fugitive and point-source emissions.
Facility or permit inventory data must not be assigned to a land parcel without explicit facility-to-parcel binding.

packages.title: Defra UK Pollutant Release and Transfer Register data sets — scope and status QA
facts: Defra last updated its UK PRTR data-set guidance on 30 June 2026.
PRTRs are inventories of pollution from industrial sites and other sources.
The register covers releases to air, water and soil and transfers off-site for treatment or disposal.
Pollutant thresholds and reporting methods are part of the register context and must be preserved.
A PRTR facility record is not automatically a parcel greenhouse-gas measurement.

packages.title: DfT Strategic charging infrastructure scheme consultation — scope and status QA
facts: DfT published the strategic charging infrastructure scheme consultation on 26 June 2026.
The consultation applies to England and concerns electricity-network infrastructure for selected motorway service areas.
The proposal is intended to enable deployment of ultra-rapid chargers where network capacity is a barrier.
A consultation proposal is not evidence that the infrastructure has already been delivered.
No emissions reduction or parcel value is treated as observed from the consultation.
